connectorUiConfig.title: Datazag Threat Intelligence
connectorUiConfig.descriptionMarkdown:
Datazag detects brand impersonation, platform impersonation and attacker infrastructure from Certificate Transparency at certificate issuance time, scores each finding, and publishes high-confidence results as STIX 2.1 indicators over a TAXII 2.1 server.

Indicators are ingested using Microsoft Sentinel's built-in **Threat Intelligence - TAXII** data connector and land in the native **ThreatIntelIndicators** table. No custom table, data collection rule or workspace function is required. Indicators are available to analytics rules and hunting queries immediately, and because they are retained in the workspace you can retro-hunt existing logs against them.

Datazag never queries your workspace. Delivery is pull-only: Sentinel polls the Datazag TAXII server on a schedule you control.

**Collections**

| Collection | Contents |
|---|---|
| `platform-alerts` | Domains impersonating widely-used platforms |
| `Infrastructure-alerts` | Hosting infrastructure associated with confirmed impersonation campaigns |

Each collection is configured as a separate TAXII server entry.

| where tostring(Data.created_by_ref) == 'identity--55a5a448-c6f1-5128-bc71-4d85b719131e'
| summarize LastReceived = max(TimeGenerated)
| project IsConnected = LastReceived > ago(3d)

connectorUiConfig.additionalRequirementBanner: Analytic rules and hunting queries in this solution query DNS activity through the [Advanced Security Information Model (ASIM)](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/sentinel/normalization). The ASIM DNS parsers must be deployed in this workspace, and the workspace must be receiving DNS telemetry, for this content to return results.

properties.description:
Matches active Datazag domain indicators against DNS query activity normalized by the ASIM
Dns schema. Reading from the ASIM parser rather than a vendor-specific table means the rule
works across any normalized DNS source in the workspace (Windows DNS, Infoblox, Cisco
Umbrella, Azure Firewall, Zscaler and others) without modification. The ASIM DNS parsers
must be deployed in the workspace for this rule to return results.

A match means a host inside the estate resolved a domain that Datazag scored as brand
impersonation, platform impersonation or attacker infrastructure at or above the configured
confidence floor. Resolution is not proof of compromise, but it establishes that the domain
reached a resolver from inside the estate, which is the earliest observable point in most
credential-phishing chains.

Indicators are identified by their STIX created_by_ref rather than by SourceSystem, because
SourceSystem reflects the friendly name chosen when the TAXII connector was configured and
therefore differs between deployments.

Indicator revisions are collapsed with arg_max by Id, so a re-derived indicator does not
produce duplicate matches. Withdrawn, revoked and expired indicators are excluded.
properties.displayName: Datazag - impersonation domain resolved in DNS
properties.query:
let datazag_identity = "identity--55a5a448-c6f1-5128-bc71-4d85b719131e";
let ioc_lookback = 14d;
let dns_lookback = 1h;
let confidence_floor = 85;
let DatazagDomains =
    ThreatIntelIndicators
    | where TimeGenerated >= ago(ioc_lookback)
    | where tostring(Data.created_by_ref) == datazag_identity
    | where ObservableKey == "domain-name:value"
    | where isnotempty(ObservableValue)
    | summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, *) by Id
    | where IsDeleted == false
    | where tostring(Data.revoked) != "true"
    | where isempty(ValidUntil) or ValidUntil > now()
    | where Confidence >= confidence_floor
    | extend IndicatorDomain = tolower(trim_end(@"\.", ObservableValue))
    | project
        IndicatorDomain,
        IndicatorStixId     = tostring(Data.id),
        IndicatorRecordId   = Id,
        DatazagAlertRef     = tostring(Data.external_references[0].external_id),
        Confidence,
        IndicatorEvidence   = tostring(Data.labels),
        IndicatorValidUntil = ValidUntil;
let DnsActivity =
    _Im_Dns
    | where TimeGenerated >= ago(dns_lookback)
    | where isnotempty(DnsQuery)
    | extend IndicatorDomain = tolower(trim_end(@"\.", DnsQuery))
    | project
        DnsTime         = TimeGenerated,
        IndicatorDomain,
        DnsQuery,
        SrcIpAddr       = column_ifexists("SrcIpAddr", ""),
        SrcHostname     = column_ifexists("SrcHostname", ""),
        SrcUsername     = column_ifexists("SrcUsername", ""),
        SrcUsernameType = column_ifexists("SrcUsernameType", ""),
        EventVendor     = column_ifexists("EventVendor", ""),
        EventProduct    = column_ifexists("EventProduct", "");
DatazagDomains
| join kind=innerunique DnsActivity on IndicatorDomain
| summarize
    FirstSeen   = min(DnsTime),
    LastSeen    = max(DnsTime),
    QueryCount  = count(),
    SourceIps   = make_set(SrcIpAddr, 50),
    SourceHosts = make_set(SrcHostname, 50),
    Upns        = make_set_if(SrcUsername, SrcUsernameType == "UPN", 50),
    SeenBy      = make_set(strcat(EventVendor, " ", EventProduct), 10)
    by
    IndicatorDomain, IndicatorStixId, IndicatorRecordId, DatazagAlertRef,
    Confidence, IndicatorEvidence, IndicatorValidUntil
| extend
    SourceIp   = tostring(SourceIps[0]),
    SourceHost = tostring(SourceHosts[0]),
    AccountUpn = tostring(Upns[0])
| order by LastSeen desc

properties.displayName: Datazag - retro-hunt historical DNS against impersonation indicators
properties.query:
let datazag_identity = "identity--55a5a448-c6f1-5128-bc71-4d85b719131e";
let dns_lookback = 90d;
let confidence_floor = 85;
let DatazagDomains =
    ThreatIntelIndicators
    | where tostring(Data.created_by_ref) == datazag_identity
    | where ObservableKey == "domain-name:value"
    | where isnotempty(ObservableValue)
    | summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, *) by Id
    | where IsDeleted == false
    | where tostring(Data.revoked) != "true"
    | where Confidence >= confidence_floor
    | extend IndicatorDomain = tolower(trim_end(@"\.", ObservableValue))
    | project
        IndicatorDomain,
        DatazagAlertRef = tostring(Data.external_references[0].external_id),
        Confidence,
        IndicatorEvidence = tostring(Data.labels),
        IndicatorFirstPublished = todatetime(Data.created);
let DnsActivity =
    _Im_Dns
    | where TimeGenerated >= ago(dns_lookback)
    | where isnotempty(DnsQuery)
    | extend IndicatorDomain = tolower(trim_end(@"\.", DnsQuery))
    | project
        DnsTime         = TimeGenerated,
        IndicatorDomain,
        SrcIpAddr       = column_ifexists("SrcIpAddr", ""),
        SrcHostname     = column_ifexists("SrcHostname", ""),
        SrcUsername     = column_ifexists("SrcUsername", ""),
        SrcUsernameType = column_ifexists("SrcUsernameType", "");
DatazagDomains
| join kind=innerunique DnsActivity on IndicatorDomain
| summarize
    FirstResolved = min(DnsTime),
    LastResolved  = max(DnsTime),
    QueryCount    = count(),
    SourceIps     = make_set(SrcIpAddr, 100),
    SourceHosts   = make_set(SrcHostname, 100),
    Upns          = make_set_if(SrcUsername, SrcUsernameType == "UPN", 100)
    by IndicatorDomain, DatazagAlertRef, Confidence, IndicatorEvidence, IndicatorFirstPublished
| extend
    SourceIp      = tostring(SourceIps[0]),
    SourceHost    = tostring(SourceHosts[0]),
    AccountUpn    = tostring(Upns[0]),
    HostsAffected = array_length(SourceHosts),
    DaysBeforeIndicator = datetime_diff('day', IndicatorFirstPublished, FirstResolved)
| order by FirstResolved asc

tags.name: description
tags.value:
Sweeps the workspace DNS history against the current Datazag indicator set to answer the
question "what did we already miss?".

This is the query to run immediately after connecting the Datazag TAXII feed. Indicators are
retained in the workspace, so they can be matched against logs that predate the connection.
A domain detected by Datazag at certificate issuance may have been resolved inside the estate
weeks before the feed was configured.

The lookback is deliberately wider than any scheduled analytic rule can use, which is why
this is a hunting query rather than a rule. Adjust dns_lookback to match your DNS retention.

If DNS logs are held in an auxiliary or data lake tier rather than the analytics tier, they
are not reachable from advanced hunting and must be queried through the data lake
exploration experience instead.

properties.descriptionHtml:
Note: Please refer to the following before installing the solution:

• Review the solution Release Notes

• There may be known issues pertaining to this Solution, please refer to them before installing.

The Datazag solution for Microsoft Sentinel delivers impersonation and attacker-infrastructure indicators derived from Certificate Transparency at issuance time, published as STIX 2.1 objects over a TAXII 2.1 server.

Indicators are ingested using Microsoft Sentinel's built-in Threat Intelligence - TAXII data connector and land in the native ThreatIntelIndicators table. No custom table, data collection rule or workspace function is required, and indicators are available to analytics rules and hunting queries immediately. Because indicators are retained in the workspace, existing logs can also be retro-hunted against them.

Prerequisites:

  1. An active Datazag subscription. Contact Datazag to obtain the API root, collection ID and credentials.

  2. Analytic rules and hunting queries in this solution query DNS activity through the Advanced Security Information Model (ASIM). The relevant ASIM parsers must be deployed in the workspace for this content to return results.

Data Connectors: 1, Analytic Rules: 1, Hunting Queries: 1
